headline: Quantum Bounds, Argmax Rounding, and Thermodynamic Limits
summary: Today's research highlights fundamental theoretical breakthroughs in quantum state estimation and entanglement limits alongside new mathematical tools for optimization. Papers introduce an argmax principle for Sum-of-Squares relaxations, resolve long-standing quantum conjectures, and establish thermodynamic constraints on open quantum engines and pseudomode dynamics.

themes.title: SoS Relaxations & Argmax Rounding
themes.body: An argmax principle for sphere optimization provides tighter bounds for Sum-of-Squares relaxations. When applied to symmetric-extension SDPs, it establishes optimal quantum de Finetti bounds and disproves Watrous's long-standing disentangler conjecture.

themes.title: Open Systems & Quantum Thermodynamics
themes.body: Investigations into open quantum dynamics show how cavity squeezing can fuel two-qubit heat engines beyond standard limits, while revealing conditions under which pseudomode models fail—or can be constructed—to reach proper thermal equilibrium.

themes.title: Quantum State Estimation & Entanglement Limits
themes.body: New foundational bounds establish near-tight ~Ω(N²) sample limits for estimating core quantum functionals like entropy and fidelity. Meanwhile, flower states demonstrate a massive operational entanglement irreversibility gap under NE operations.

connections.body: Paper 2608.02590 directly utilizes the argmax principle for Sum-of-Squares relaxations introduced in 2608.02594 to round symmetric-extension SDPs, yielding optimal quantum de Finetti bounds.
Both 2608.02521 and 2608.02517 address thermodynamic consistency in open quantum systems, evaluating non-Markovian bath interactions and detailed balance conditions.
